question: How does introducing Na-ion vacancies and halogen doping affect the conductivity of Na3PS4, and which dopant is most effective?
answer: Introducing Na-ion vacancies and halogen doping significantly enhances the conductivity of Na3PS4 by increasing Na-vacancy concentration and facilitating ion diffusion. DFT MD simulations show that just 2% Na-ion vacancies raise the conductivity by an order of magnitude (0.20 S/cm) while lowering the activation energy from 0.28 to 0.16 eV. Among halogen dopants, Br-doping is most effective, further boosting conductivity by optimizing vacancy formation. Phonon-induced free volume also aids diffusion by improving Na-ion transition rates between sites. Both cubic and tetragonal phases exhibit similar high conductivity, but grain boundary resistance remains a limiting factor in macroscopic performance. The metastable Na2-site occupancy increases with higher vacancy concentrations and temperature, confirming the role of vacancies in enhancing Na1 → Na1 transitions.

The purpose of the paper is to use density functional theory (DFT) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the Na-ion conductivity of cubic and tetragonal Na3PS4. The study identifies mechanisms to enhance Na-ion conductivity, including the introduction of Na-ion vacancies and halogen doping (e.g., Br-doping). Additionally, the paper explores the role of vacancies, phonons, and grain boundary resistance in determining macroscopic conductivity.
